level_1: Consistently obtains complete, accurate, and relevant general psychiatry history and mental status and describes a functional assessment
Performs the neurocognitive assessment
Interprets collateral information and test results to determine necessary additional steps in the evaluation, while preserving patient autonomy

Integrates findings from neurocognitive assessment with other clinical data
level_3: Describes the elements of neurocognitive assessment
Interprets collateral information and test results to determine necessary additional steps
Serves as a role model for gathering subtle and accurate findings from the patient and collateral sources
level_4: Obtains complete and relevant geriatric psychiatry history and mental status and performs a comprehensive functional assessment
Interprets the findings from the neurocognitive assessment and refers for neuropsychological testing, as indicated
Serves as a leader for neurocognitive testing, evaluation, and interpretation for treatment planning by the patient care team
level_5: Orders appropriate additional laboratory and diagnostic tests, including and neuroimaging
Integrates and synthesizes history, clinical data, and functional assessment to determine necessary additional steps in the evaluation

level_1: Identifies information from relevant sources to develop a basic differential diagnosis for common geriatric patient presentations
Engages in a basic risk assessment and basic safety planning
Develops formulations based on multiple conceptual models
level_2: Describes the role of biological, psychosocial, cultural, and developmental/life cycle factors for a geriatric patient

Incorporates risk and protective factors into the assessment of complex patient presentations, including eliciting information not readily offered by the patient
level_3: Screens for safety and risk of harm to oneself, to others, or by others
Synthesizes all information into a concise but comprehensive formulation, taking into account biological, psychosocial, cultural, and developmental/life cycle factors
Serves as a role model in the development of accurate and complete differential diagnoses and formulations
level_4: Integrates information from relevant sources to develop a basic differential diagnosis for common geriatric patient presentations
Incorporates risk and protective factors into the assessment of imminent, short-, and long-term patient safety and the safety of others
Serves as a role model for safety and risk assessment
level_5: Identifies the specific biological, psychosocial, cultural, and developmental /life cycle factors that contribute to a geriatric patient’s presentation
Develops differential diagnoses in complex cases and incorporates subtle, unusual, or conflicting findings

level_1: Applies knowledge of the general principles of psychopharmacology
Applies principles of geriatric psychopharmacology and treatment response in the selection and management of somatic therapies
Integrates behavioral and environmental setting intervention appropriately with other treatment modalities
level_2: Establishes and maintains a therapeutic alliance and professional boundaries while providing psychotherapies to patients with uncomplicated problems
Integrates the selected psychotherapy with other treatment modalities and other providers of care
Explains less common somatic treatment choices to patients and patient families in terms of proposed mechanisms of action
level_3: Applies knowledge of the geriatric psychopharmacology principles
Provides behavioral and environmental interventions when clinically appropriate
Integrates emerging studies of geriatric therapeutic modalities into clinical practice
level_4: Establishes and maintains a therapeutic alliance with older adults
Selects and manages appropriate psychopharmacologic and other somatic treatment options in patients with significant medical comorbidities and treatment refractory disorders
level_5: Identifies behavioral and environmental factors that impact psychiatric presentations
Selects a psychotherapeutic modality and tailors the selected psychotherapy to the patient based on an appropriate case formulation

level_1: Establishes treatment goals with the patient
Recognizes the cultural factors and social determinants of health impacting the care of geriatric patients
Consistently identifies and manages patient safety issues and comorbid substance use and medical conditions while utilizing consultation for refractory cases or complicated cases
level_2: Recognizes geriatric patient in crises, acute, or chronic presentation of psychiatric and medical conditions
Devises and modifies, as needed, individualized patient-centered treatment plans for common presentations
Provides comprehensive management of multiple and complex conditions, while addressing social determinants of health
level_3: Recognizes cultural factors and social determinants of health impacting the care of all patients
Manages patients’ comorbid conditions, such as substance use and medical problems related to the psychiatric presentation, treatment, and prognosis, utilizing consultation services
Supervises treatment planning of other learners and multidisciplinary care practitioners
level_4: Identifies additional disciplines to address treatment goals specific to the needs of a geriatric patient
Provides sensitive and culturally aware care to socioeconomically disadvantaged patients
Creates and leads a comprehensive patient - centered management plan for the patient with highly complex conditions, safety issues, medical, and substance use comorbidities
level_5: Manages geriatric patient in crises, acute, or chronic presentation with supervision using appropriate interventions

level_1: Uses the EHR for routine patient care activities
Adjusts interview and cognitive evaluation to address technological difficulties and patient needs and preferences
level_2: Describes potential benefits, challenges, and appropriate clinical usage of telehealth visits for older adults
Supports an interdisciplinary care team through the use of the EHR and asynchronous communication
level_3: Accesses secondary data sources for use in patient care activities
Recognizes and evaluates complex physical and mental status exam findings via video visit
level_4: Performs assigned telehealth visits using approved technology, including establishing therapeutic alliance and, obtaining basic history and mental status exam
Leads improvements to the EHR
level_5: Effectively manages therapeutic relationship through virtual environment and asynchronous communication
Develops and innovates new ways to use emerging technologies to augment telehealth visits

level_1: Describes physiological changes associated with normal aging and developmental theories of later life
Demonstrates basic knowledge of the role of cultural context and social determinants in later life
Analyzes and discusses the influence of pathological and environmental factors on later life
level_2: Describes the influence of biological, psychosocial, and cultural factors on personality development
Identifies major deviations from typical later-life development
Evaluates the impact of life events, functional change, and general medical health on the expression of psychopathology in later life
level_3: Describes common life events, functional change, and general medical conditions occurring in later life
Describes the impact of pathological and environmental factors on later life
Incorporates new scientific knowledge into understanding of later- life development
level_4: Applies developmental theories to explain transitions in later life
Describes the impact of cultural context and social determinants on mental health conditions occurring in later life.
level_5: Identifies pathological and environmental factors that commonly occur in later life and may impact later-life development
Incorporates knowledge of later-life development into the clinical formulation

level_1: Demonstrates sufficient knowledge to identify and treat most psychiatric conditions throughout the life cycles

Diagnoses complex clinical conditions in geriatric psychiatric patients in collaboration with other clinical disciplines
level_3: Demonstrates knowledge of screening and evaluation tools to identify psychiatric conditions in the general medical patient population
Recognizes the impact of functional and neurocognitive impairments on safety in older adults
Teaches risk assessment and determination of level of care for geriatric patients
level_4: Demonstrates sufficient knowledge to identify and treat common psychiatric conditions in later life
Recognizes medical conditions in geriatric psychiatry patients in collaboration with other clinical disciplines
Develops protocols for risk assessment and determination of appropriate level of care in collaboration with other clinical disciplines
level_5: Weighs the risk and protective factors in older adults and determines the appropriate level of care

level_1: Demonstrates an evidence-based understanding of psychotropic and somatic treatment modalities for common psychiatric disorders

Critically appraises the evidence for efficacy of non-pharmacological therapies with and without concomitant pharmacotherapy

level_3: Describes characteristics of various treatment settings and models of care

level_1: Describes common patient safety events

level_2: Describes process of patient safety event reporting
Participates in analysis of patient safety events (simulated or actual)

level_3: Discusses basic quality improvement methodologies and metrics

Participates in quality improvement initiatives

level_1: Demonstrates knowledge of care coordination

subcompetencies.name: Physician Role in Health Care Systems

level_1: Identifies key components of the complex health care system

level_3: Identifies basic concepts for effective transition to fellowship

level_5: Identifies barriers to care in different health care systems

level_1: Recognizes issues of self-determination and lists criteria for decisional capacity in a patient

level_1: Demonstrates how to access and summarize available evidence for routine conditions

level_3: Locates and applies the best available evidence to the care of patients applying a hierarchy of evidence

subcompetencies.name: Reflective Practice and Commitment to Personal Growth

level_1: Accepts responsibility for personal and professional development by establishing goals

level_2: Identifies the factors that contribute to gap(s) between one’s expected and actual performance
Seeks performance data episodically, with openness and humility

level_4: Demonstrates openness to performance data (feedback and other input) to inform goals

level_5: Analyzes and reflects on the factors that contribute to gap(s) between one’s expected and actual performance
Intentionally seeks performance data consistently, with openness and humility

level_1: Identifies and describes core professional behavior
Analyzes straightforward situations using ethical principles
Responds appropriately to professionalism lapses of colleagues

level_4: Demonstrates professional behavior in routine situations
Analyzes complex situations using ethical principles and recognizes when help is needed

level_1: Takes responsibility to complete tasks and responsibilities, identifies potential contributing factors for lapses, and describes strategies for ensuring timely task completion in the future

level_1: Recognizes the importance of addressing personal and professional well-being

level_3: Describes institutional resources designed to promote well-being

level_1: Uses language and non- verbal communication to demonstrate empathic curiosity, respect, and to establish rapport

level_2: Identifies common barriers to effective communication; accurately communicates one’s own role within the health care system

level_1: Uses language that values all members of the health care team

level_3: Communicates information effectively with all health care team members

level_4: Solicits feedback on performance as a member of the health care team

level_1: Accurately records information in the patient record

level_2: Safeguards patient personal health information
Concisely reports diagnostic and therapeutic reasoning in the patient record
Initiates difficult conversations with appropriate stakeholders to improve the system
level_3: Communicates about administrative issues through appropriate channels, as required by institutional policy

level_4: Demonstrates organized diagnostic and therapeutic reasoning through notes in the patient record

level_5: Uses documentation shortcuts accurately and appropriately to enhance efficiency of communication
